summary:
Democrats won control of the House and Senate in the US midterm elections on Tuesday, flipping Senate seats in Texas, Iowa, Kansas, North Carolina, South Carolina and Ohio, with many seats still uncounted. Trump said he would accept the results and acknowledged that "a part of it was Iran" in his party's losses. In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim US senator.

Trump said the US will end military aid to Israel at the end of this year, a sum reported as $3.8 billion in one account and nearly $4 billion in others, while still selling weapons to Israel. In Israel, the Central Elections Committee rejected fraud claims made by Benjamin Netanyahu against Arab parties after auditing 9,069 polling stations. Netanyahu's allies refused to back the result, and President Isaac Herzog has begun talks on who should form the next government.

In Spain, Transport Minister Oscar Puente resigned on Tuesday after a high-speed train crash south of Madrid killed 69 people, though another report says nearly 70. It was the second high-speed rail accident in the country in less than a year. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez faces a snap poll this month.

headlines.title: Democrats win control of US House and Senate in midterms
headlines.summary: Democrats won control of the House and Senate on Tuesday, flipping Senate seats in Texas, Iowa, Kansas, North Carolina, South Carolina and Ohio, with many seats still uncounted. Trump said he would accept the results and that "a part of it was Iran."

headlines.title: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race, becoming first Muslim senator
headlines.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers for Michigan's open Senate seat, becoming the first Muslim US senator. The race was marked by Islamophobic attacks from Trump and Republican allies, and Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary, backed Rogers at the last minute.

headlines.title: Trump says US will end military aid to Israel this year
headlines.summary: Trump said the US will end military aid to Israel at the end of this year, a sum reported as $3.8 billion in one account and nearly $4 billion in others. He said the US would still sell weapons to Israel.

headlines.title: Israeli election body rejects Netanyahu's fraud claims
headlines.summary: The Central Elections Committee rejected fraud claims by Benjamin Netanyahu against Arab parties, saying an audit of 9,069 polling stations confirmed the announced results. Netanyahu's allies refused to back the result, and President Isaac Herzog has begun talks on who should form the next government.

headlines.title: Spain's transport minister resigns after train crash kills 69
headlines.summary: Oscar Puente resigned on Tuesday after a high-speed train crash south of Madrid killed 69 people, though another report says nearly 70. It was the second high-speed rail accident in Spain in less than a year, and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez faces a snap poll this month.

headlines.title: Bomb threats force checks on seven flights across Europe
headlines.summary: Authorities are investigating threats against at least seven planes in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy. The aircraft all landed safely, and searches on the ground found no explosives.

headlines.title: South Africa holds local elections, with ANC expected to lose ground
headlines.summary: South Africans vote on Wednesday, November 4, in local elections, with the ANC expected to win less than a third of the vote amid anger over water outages and power cuts. Ballot storage facilities were targeted and arrests were made across several provinces, and the Electoral Commission has tightened security.

headlines.title: Sweden's central bank and Australian banks raise interest rates
headlines.summary: Sweden's central bank raised its key interest rate for the first time since the war between the US and Iran began, and signaled that more increases are likely. Australian banks said they will raise their own rates after the Reserve Bank of Australia lifted the cash rate for the fifth time in 2026.
